one_line: A piano-learning page that lights the next key and lets an agent hear and grade play on the same piano.
what_it_does: Guides learners through notes, chords, and songs using glowing keys, input from click/keyboard/MIDI, and agent-controlled drills.
leverage_rationale: The agent shares live keyboard state and can light and grade the exact next key; a generic UI-driving agent would have materially less reliable access to musical input and feedback.
leverage_evidence: Pitch and description say the next key glows and the agent hears the same piano.
Tools include set-next-keys and agent-created drills.
Supports click, typing, and MIDI input with miss feedback.
execution_rationale: The written workflow is coherent and detailed, but the packet has no transcript and the visual evidence could not be inspected, so end-to-end completion remains claimed rather than demonstrated.
execution_evidence: Description specifies teach, play, miss feedback, hear, harmonize, and named lessons.
Demo is reported alive and one gallery image is reported.
impact_rationale: Beginning piano learners have a clear need for immediate, embodied feedback; the product addresses the common uncertainty of which key to play and whether it was correct.
impact_evidence: Explicit beginner-learning use case.
Lessons include first keys, scales, chords, and recognizable songs.
creativity_rationale: It makes the shared human-agent state physical and musical: the agent does not merely say a note but lights it and evaluates the learner's actual playing.
creativity_evidence: Glow-first interaction model and same-page listening.
Agent can invent drills while the human plays.
usability_note: Potentially approachable because the next action is visual, though hardware/MIDI availability may limit some users.
red_flags: No video transcript; visual proof unavailable due to image-analysis rate limit.
standouts: Strong embodied use of shared WebMCP state.
advance_reason: Distinctive agent-plus-instrument interaction with a credible learner benefit; advance subject to observed execution verification.

one_line: An ERP where an agent drafts and queries shared business state while a human retains approval of irreversible accounting actions.
what_it_does: Provides SME ERP workflows for quotes, orders, shipping, accounting, invoicing, VAT, and HR with structured agent tools and human approval gates.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP is central: structured reports, live drafts, shared view state, and approval-gated submission address the reliability and auditability problems of agents operating dense ERP screens.
leverage_evidence: Agent can query real ledger numbers without scraping or menu navigation.
draft_quote writes a live editable card and get_current_view reads the same draft.
submit_draft suspends for human approval before irreversible commit.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a broad but internally coherent ERP and a carefully designed draft-to-human-approval workflow; no video is submitted, so the score is execution claimed rather than observed.
execution_evidence: Live judge demo is reported alive with explicit credentials.
Description covers multiple ERP domains and a concrete draft/approval flow.
Public repository and hackathon-period provenance are stated.
impact_rationale: Taiwanese SMEs have a real need for reliable ERP operation and accounting accuracy; shared drafts and human approval directly reduce costly agent errors.
impact_evidence: Specific SME audience and business workflows.
Human retains final approval for posting to books.
Ledger, tax, inventory, and payroll use cases are consequential.
creativity_rationale: The agent-as-drafter/human-as-approver model is a thoughtful interaction pattern for high-stakes enterprise software, beyond simply exposing CRUD tools.
creativity_evidence: Approval by structure and live shared draft editing.
Same-screen agent and human collaboration across ERP state.
usability_note: Structured tools and visible drafts improve safety, but ERP breadth and login setup add complexity.
red_flags: No submitted video frames could be visually verified.
standouts: Strong human-approval boundary for irreversible accounting actions.
advance_reason: Exceptional WebMCP fit and high-stakes practical value; advance strongly, with live observation as the remaining verification.

one_line: A one-script builder that scans portfolios, maps capabilities, installs WebMCP, and verifies the live integration.

leverage_evidence: Seventeen tools cover designs, elements, generation, background removal, restyling, export, and memory.
Every edit lands in a pending batch and nothing commits until approval.

execution_rationale: The described product has a coherent end-to-end creation and approval loop with a concrete implementation stack and protocol feed; visual frames are unavailable for verification.
execution_evidence: Public repo and live demo are reported.

impact_rationale: Small businesses, creators, and social marketers have a concrete need for fast promotional graphics while retaining editorial control; this addresses both production and oversight.
impact_evidence: Explicit flyers, posters, and social-post audience/use cases.

creativity_rationale: The pending-batch protocol and tool lifecycle events make consent and collaboration first-class in a creative canvas, not a bolt-on confirmation dialog.

red_flags: No visual verification available for the submitted frame sheets.
standouts: Best consent-aware creative collaboration model in the packet.
advance_reason: High leverage, strong product coherence, and memorable approval semantics warrant advancement.
